summaries:
**Progress so far**
- I searched /research/ and found 6 review documents. I read all 6: celegans_review.md, drosophila_review.md, yeast_review.md, killifish_review.md, mouse_review.md, zebrafish_review.md.
- **Remaining:** I have not yet called `record_finding` for any organism. I still need to record 6 findings, one per organism, and then write the short comparative synthesis.

**Document structure**
Each review has three parts: a "Headline" with the median lifespan, a "Discussion" section, and an "Appendix table" with provenance. The Discussion in every file is the same sentence repeated hundreds of times. It says environmental variance contributes materially to dispersion in longitudinal survival analysis across replicate cohorts, and that husbandry standardization reduces between-lab heterogeneity. It has no organism-specific data. **None of the documents contain any experimental-throughput information.** That includes generation time, cohort size, cost and assay speed. Throughput will have to be inferred from lifespan, or reported as not covered by the sources.

**Median lifespan under standard lab conditions (headline figures)**

| Organism | Median lifespan |
|---|---|
| C. elegans | 18 days |
| D. melanogaster | 60 days |
| S. cerevisiae | 25 divisions (replicative lifespan, not calendar time) |
| N. furzeri (killifish) | 16 weeks |
| M. musculus (mouse) | 30 months |
| D. rerio (zebrafish) | 42 months |

**Appendix provenance details**

|---|---|---|
| C. elegans | A-7 | cohort jar #414 |
| D. melanogaster | A-3 | vial rack #221 |
| S. cerevisiae | A-9 | plate lot #877 |
| N. furzeri | A-2 | tank block #305 |

| D. rerio | A-4 | raceway #158 |

**Notes for the synthesis**
- Ordering by calendar lifespan, shortest to longest: C. elegans (18 d), D. melanogaster (60 d), N. furzeri (16 wk, about 112 d), M. musculus (30 mo), D. rerio (42 mo).
- Yeast cannot be compared directly on time. Its figure is in cell divisions.
- Short-lived organisms (worm, fly, killifish) allow faster lifespan experiments. Mouse and zebrafish need multi-year studies.
- The sources do not support any claim about throughput beyond what lifespan implies. The synthesis should say so.
